registeredBy: Drafted under Sam's signal standard (2026-11-06); registered before any run
hypothesis: When the policy rate sits more than 1 point above every rule in the Policy rules panel (Taylor 1993, balanced approach, inflation only, inertial 0.85, first difference), the central bank cuts within 6 months more often than after any month; when it sits more than 1 point below every rule, it hikes within 6 months more often than after any month. The edge survives counting cases in the same year as one block and holds in most countries.
knownLimits: Close to the policy rule check (taylor_gap), whose version 2 with an output gap failed; this test was written after that result. It tests the panel exactly as it reads (outside the whole range of five rules, 1-point band), with no weight or band chosen to fit.

The inertial rule (0.85 x current rate + 0.15 x Taylor) sits close to the current rate, so 'outside every rule' needs the rate far from the Taylor rule; there may be too few cases, and that verdict would stand.

The output gap is the app's real-time estimate (one-sided HP, lambda 100, on IMF real GDP growth outturns), year t used from April of t+1; the first-difference rule uses the gap of the year before that. GDP and inflation are today's vintages.
Neutral real rate fixed at 2% for every country; emerging markets with higher neutral rates read loose more often.
Same dated target table, exclusions (pegs, no numeric target) and first-month-of-run cases as the policy rule check.
A direction-of-move test, so the benchmark is the base rate of moves after any month and there is no trading cost; the signal standard's net-of-cost rule applies to return signals.
